verses.text: Simon Peter, a servant and apostle of Jesus Christ, to those who received a faith as precious as ours through the righteousness of our God and Savior Jesus Christ:
May grace and peace be multiplied to you through knowing God and Jesus our Lord.
His divine power has given us everything we need for life and godliness through knowing the one who called us by his own glory and goodness.
Through these he has given us his precious and very great promises, so that through them you may share in the divine nature and escape the world’s corruption caused by evil desires.
For this very reason, make every effort to add goodness to your faith, knowledge to goodness,
self-control to knowledge, endurance to self-control, godliness to endurance,
mutual affection to godliness, and love to mutual affection.
If these qualities are yours and keep growing, they’ll keep you from being ineffective or unfruitful in knowing our Lord Jesus Christ.
Whoever lacks them is shortsighted and blind, forgetting that they’ve been cleansed from past sins.
So, brothers and sisters, make every effort to confirm that God has called and chosen you. If you do these things, you’ll never fall.
Then you’ll be richly welcomed into the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.
That’s why I’ll always remind you about these things, even though you know them and are firmly established in the truth you have.
I think it’s right to keep refreshing your memory as long as I’m alive in this tent of a body,
because I know I’ll soon put it aside, as our Lord Jesus Christ has made clear to me.
I’ll make every effort so that after my departure you’ll always be able to remember these things.
We didn’t follow cleverly made-up stories when we told you about the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ. We saw his majesty with our own eyes.
He received honor and glory from God the Father when the voice came to him from the Majestic Glory, saying, “This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased.”
We heard that voice come from heaven when we were with him on the holy mountain.
We also have the prophetic message made more certain, and you’ll do well to pay attention to it, like a lamp shining in a dark place, until day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts.
First of all, understand this: no prophecy of Scripture comes from the prophet’s own interpretation.
Prophecy never came from human will. Instead, people spoke from God as they were carried along by the Holy Spirit.
